extracted.intended_audience: novice lady riders / beginners learning equitation
extracted.subtask_description: Practical instructional guidance for young ladies learning to ride: mounting, basic aids, walking/trotting/cantering, stopping, leaping, dismounting, and lesson management. Emphasises balance, correct aids, gentle animations, and progressive practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing and correcting rearing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a horse rears, slacken the reins, bend the body forward to throw weight on his shoulders; when his fore-feet come to the ground, having recovered position, correct him smartly or pull him round two or three times to divert him from his object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rider may anticipate rearing and adopt the latter (pull-round) course to prevent it. While holding the horse's head up to prevent kicking, avoid so much pressure on the mouth as to cause rearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling attempted throwing or head-down runs
rubrics_metrics.description: If, when unprepared, the horse gets his head down, the rider must try, by means of the reins, to prevent the animal from throwing himself, and by inclining the body backward save herself from being thrown forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If opportunity occurs, give the horse two or three sharp turns to divert him; this also helps if the horse shows incipient attempts to kick.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing kicking tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: A horse that displays any symptoms of kicking should be held tight in hand; while his head is well kept up, he cannot do much mischief with his heels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold the head up and keep a firm hand; however, don't hold so strongly as to induce rearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a quiet, well-trained horse and careful attendant for beginners
rubrics_metrics.description: A quiet and well-trained horse, and a careful attendant, should, if possible, be procured; a horse that knows his duty will almost instruct his rider; a friend or careful servant accompanying the pupil reduces risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginners who cannot take lessons from a master should rely on a calm mount and an experienced helper to materially assist progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary study of mounting, aids and position
rubrics_metrics.description: Before aspiring to ride, pupils should attentively read and practise the directions on Mounting, the Aids, and proper disposition of body and limbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fundamentals should be practised gradually in early lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walk: head up, reins not too tight, feel the cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the pupil walk the horse forward in a straight line at a slow rate, supporting his head so as to make him keep time; but not holding the reins so tight as to impede the measurement of his steps or to make him break into a trot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold the hand so as to delicately but distinctly feel, by the horse's mouth on the reins, every beat of his action; relax the hand the moment he drops into a walk after a check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animating the horse gently to maintain gait
rubrics_metrics.description: If the horse does not exert himself sufficiently, he should be somewhat animated; animations during the first lessons should be commenced with great gentleness and increased only as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too strong an animation will raise the horse's courage and may alarm the rider; increase animations gradually and discover by experience how much is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking an unwanted trot from the walk
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the horse break into a trot, he must be checked by the reins; the pull must neither be so firm nor continued as to make him stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As soon as he obeys and drops back to a walk, relax the hand; if he again requires animating, use a gentler movement than before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turning: coordinated use of each rein and hand alternation
rubrics_metrics.description: When pulling the right rein to turn right, the other hand must be relaxed and lowered or advanced to slacken the left rein and ease the horse's mouth, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate use of both hands is to be practised; if the horse does not readily obey in turning or bring forward his croup, urge him to throw himself on the bit by leg or whip animation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animations to bring the croup forward
rubrics_metrics.description: If the horse will not bring his croup sufficiently forward, he must be urged to throw himself more on the bit by an animation of the leg or whip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin animations gently in early lessons and increase only as needed for obedience and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inner rein and body inclination when riding circles
rubrics_metrics.description: In riding round a circle, the inner rein should be rather lowered, and the body inclined inward; this inclination must be increased as the circle is contracted and the pace quickens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inside rein should be alternately borne on slightly and then relaxed, the hand keeping exact time with the cadence of the horse's feet; avoid jerking or bearing steadily without intermission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deadening the horse's mouth with improper rein action
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inner rein be jerked at intervals the horse will swerve in and out; if borne upon without intermission the rider's hand and the animal's mouth will become deadened and correspondence decreased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use delicate, timed alternation of bearing and relaxing to procure correct action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice both directions equally
rubrics_metrics.description: Direction is to be frequently changed; the pupil should alternately work to the right and left to bring both hands into practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures balanced development of aids and seat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of double circles and figure-of-8 exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: After confirming seat and balance, begin to ride double circles (figure-of-8), initially large and then contracting them; vary number and size of circles to exercise balance, aids and horse obedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variety prevents mechanical performance and benefits both horse and rider; ensure mastery of a simpler figure before adding more complicated variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology and progressive combination of figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Volt = working on a circle; changes reverse = angles/zig-zag; demi-volt = half circle from a line. Figures may be performed separately then combined (e.g., demi-volt and changes reverse embodied in circle exercises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform variations ad libitum but master one figure with accuracy before proceeding to a more complicated one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting change defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the horse, in changing, yield his head but withhold his croup so as to destroy union of action, the rider should restore proper position by an aid of the whip or leg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate aids to re-establish sequence of movement during changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trot: commencement aids and controlling excessive speed
rubrics_metrics.description: To make the horse advance from a walk to a trot, draw upwards the little finger(s) and turn towards the body; accompany with an animation of the leg or whip. If the horse starts too rapidly, check him by closing the hands firmly or by drawing the little fingers upwards and towards the body, delicately and gradually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jerks; as soon as effect is produced relax reins. Repeat animations if horse does not bring up his haunches sufficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving balance and acquiring the rise in trotting
rubrics_metrics.description: When the horse in trot raises the rider from her seat, she should advance her body and rest weight on the right knee while bearing the left foot on the stirrup to return to position without being jerked; use right knee and left foot similarly to assist the rise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rising to the left (a common bad habit) and avoid rising too high; maintain seat as close as comfort allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canter: how to strike into canter and its nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Canter may be commenced from a short animated trot, a walk, or even a stop. Slight pressure of whip and leg and an elevation of the horse's head by the reins will make him strike into a canter. The perfection of canter consists in union and animation rather than speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If horse merely increases walk or goes into trot, press him forward on the bit with increased leg/whip while holding reins more firmly to prevent advancing too rapidly; practise circles in canter after proficiency in trot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn trot before attempting canter
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners who practise without a master often begin canter before trot, but it is recommended the lady first practise the trot as it better strengthens and confirms balance and seat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a progression: walk → trot → canter, improving aids and balance at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct canter lead and remedy for wrong lead
rubrics_metrics.description: The horse ought to lead with the right foot. If he strikes off with the left (wrong lead), the rider must either check him to a walk and make him recommence or induce the proper leg by acting on the near rein, pressing his side with the left leg, and touching his right shoulder with the whip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure hind legs follow fore legs; if they do not, the pace is false and should be rectified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid galloping on the road
rubrics_metrics.description: No lady of taste ever gallops on the road; gallop is only for the field and not urged on the road.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally do not permit the horse to break into a gallop except in appropriate field situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect stop: definition and correct execution
rubrics_metrics.description: The perfect stop in a pace is a cessation of all action in the animal, produced instantaneously by the rider without previous intimation to the horse. The slovenly stop is gradual and uncertain; the incorrect stop is a momentary violent check in the middle of the cadence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase firmness of the hand, throw the body back, draw the reins to the body, and press the horse's haunches forward by leg and whip so he bears on the bit; time the action to conclude with the cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing the stop in different paces
rubrics_metrics.description: Stop in the walk: conclude correctly with the cadence. Stop in the trot: operate when advanced limbs have come to the ground so the stop is perfected when the other fore and hind leg advance and complete the cadence. Stop in the canter: time at the instant when the horse's fore feet are descending; hind feet will immediately follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In an extended canter, reduce to a short trot before stopping or perform a 'double arret' (stopping in two cadences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Backing (making the horse back)
rubrics_metrics.description: To make a horse 'back' in walking, the reins must be drawn equally and steadily towards the body, and the croup kept in proper direction by means of the leg and whip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use steady, equal rein action and maintain croup alignment with leg/whip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaping: benefits and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaping (standing or flying) is beneficial to confirm the seat and preserve balance. Standing leap is from halt close to the bar; flying leap is taken from any pace and is easier, though standing is safer to begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with low bars that fall if touched; raise gradually. Use assistant help and progress only as rider improves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaping: rider position and aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not bear weight on the stirrup; press legs (particularly right) closely against the saddle; yield the reins so as to feel slight correspondence between hand and horse's mouth; advance forward as fore quarters ascend and incline body backward a moment before hind legs leave ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid leaning forward in flying leaps; bring waist forward and allow body to take the inclination backward produced by the horse's spring. After clearing, bring horse together if disunited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper run-up distance for a leap
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper distance for a horse to run previous to the leap is from ten to fifteen yards; animate an indolent animal into a short, collected gallop and urge him by strong aids to make the leap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow well-trained horses to take their own pace; ensure collected pace for an indolent horse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismounting: prepare with a perfect stop and proper rein handling
rubrics_metrics.description: First preparatory operation is to bring the horse to an easy, yet perfect, stop. Right hand receives the reins and is carried to the off crutch; reins held sufficiently tight to restrain the horse but not so firm as to make him back or rear nor uneven to make him swerve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rein-handling steps are initial for both assisted and unassisted dismounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismounting: assisted methods
rubrics_metrics.description: If assisted, the gentleman or groom may lift her off the saddle, or take her left hand and place his right on her waist to support descent; he may stand at the horse's shoulder to receive her right hand and help her alight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistants should support until rider is perfectly safe on the ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismounting: unassisted method and landing
rubrics_metrics.description: If dismounting without assistance, turn so as to take a lock of the horse's mane in left hand and, bearing right hand on the crutch, alight facing the horse's side; bend knees, keep body pliant, and alight on toes or middle of feet without relinquishing hold until safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice mounting/dismounting frequently to gain grace and facility; begin with simple modes and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression of tack and hand use
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform first lessons with a snaffle bridle, holding reins in both hands and without a stirrup. After acquiring balance and aids, use a bridle with double reins and hold them in the left hand as directed earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change tack and rein technique only after sufficient practice and confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule: proceed steadily and avoid overreaching
rubrics_metrics.description: If but in noviciate, do not place too much reliance on own expertness or attempt too much at first; proceed steadily and be satisfied with gradual improvement as perfection in niceties cannot precede overcoming minor difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conservative, progressive learning is emphasised for safety and skill acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage lesson duration and rest for the horse
rubrics_metrics.description: The time occupied in each lesson should be in proportion to the pace and animation. If exercise is varied and highly animated, the horse should rest to recruit himself after 12 or 15 minutes; refreshed, he may do another similar (or shorter) lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two halts in the same space of time are better; total animated work equal to three hours' moderate work is suggested. When lessons are less animated they may be longer; err on the side of brevity rather than overwork the horse.
